Items.Authors: Thanet Henghiran, Chitphon Kaewsaikum, Thitiya Ritkamrop, Chantira Boonsri, Nuttakrit Somdock, Thanawit Anuwongpinij, Piyamas Choochalerm, Sasithorn Hoprasong
Items.Title: Optimizing environmental stability in the EXOhSPEC spectrograph via real-time monitoring and feedback control
Items.Abstract: The primary goal was to develop an in-house enclosure for the EXOhSPEC at the Sirindhorn Astronomical Park to achieve the high thermal and environmental stability required for sub-m/s RV precision. This stability is critical for the main scientific application of the spectrograph. We enhanced stability using multi-layer thermal isolation and a custom Internet of Things (IoT) control system. This system utilizes a PID controller to drive DIY Peltier modules and actively monitors critical parameters (temperature, humidity, pressure) via integrated sensors. Real-time data is managed by an open-source dashboard. Validation showed the system successfully maintained temperature at a mean of 21.64∘C(SD±0.30∘C) and humidity at a mean of 48.20% RH. This environmental stability minimizes mechanical flexure and refractive index variation, resulting in significant enhancement for high-precision spectroscopy.

Items.Authors: Rhonda M. Morgan, Renyu Hu, Mario Damiano, Michael Turmon, Dmitry Savransky, Eric Mamajek, Bertrand Mennesson, Tyler D. Robinson, Armen Tokadjian
Items.Title: Optimizing HWO architectures for distinguishing sub-Neptune size planets as rocky planets, water worlds, or mini-Neptunes from NUV to NIR wavelengths
Items.Abstract: Sub-Neptune-sized planets are among the most common in our galaxy, yet it is currently unknown what fraction of sub-Neptune sized planets are rocky planets, water worlds, or gas-dominated mini-Neptunes. In addition to helping understand exoplanet formation and diversity, some larger-than-Earth planets with solid surfaces or oceans could support life. The Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) could perform atmospheric characterization to distinguish types of sub-Neptunes. We evaluate exoplanet characterization yields for sub-Neptunes utilizing our framework to perform a significant number of end-to-end yield simulations in a multivariate parameter sweep in the NUV, Visible, and NIR. By exploring the wavelength range and spectral quality over a broad architecture space, the multivariate parameter sensitivity reveals the intricacies within the trade space and helps to inform high level science performance requirements for the HWO Solar Systems in Context Working Group.

Items.Authors: Stefan Thoms, Martin Timpe
Items.Title: Optimizing wavefront-deformation sensor placement for active radio-telescope surfaces
Items.Abstract: A general optimization framework is presented for determining efficient placement of surface-deformation sensors on radio-telescope reflectors. Using telescope-specific finite-element load cases, the method identifies sensor configurations that maximize deformation-field reconstructability across relevant operational conditions. The approach enables both performance evaluation for a fixed sensor budget and determination of the minimum number and distribution of sensors required to meet a specified accuracy target, supporting next-generation active-surface radio telescopes.

Items.Authors: Julien Storm, Jake Pember, Gert Raskin, Christian Schwab, Nick Binos, Louis Storm
Items.Title: Optomechanical considerations for extreme thermo-mechanical stability: insights from the MARVEL high resolution echelle spectrograph
Items.Abstract: The MARVEL spectrograph is designed to deliver extreme precision radial velocity (EPRV) measurements over time series that extend across months and years. Achieving this performance requires instrument stability at the level of ≤13 nm, equivalent to 1 m/s RV precision. Therefore, MARVEL is housed in vacuum and relies on an optomechanical design that minimizes deformations and mechanical stress while incorporating alignment mechanisms engineered for long-term stability. Here we describe the kinematic mounting approaches, flexure implementations, and overall optomechanical design choices that together will enable MARVEL to maintain extreme thermo mechanical stability and nanometer scale invariance over years of operation.

Items.Authors: Devika K. Divakar, Phillip MacQueen, Andrew Pinckney, Joseph Strubhar
Items.Title: Optomechanical design of an ADC and image rotator for the HJST Coudé Spectrograph at McDonald Observatory
Items.Abstract: High-resolution spectroscopy with the Harlan J. Smith 2.7 m Telescope (HJST) benefits from stable image quality and controlled atmospheric refraction. We present the design of a Rotational Atmospheric Dispersion Corrector (RADC) and a Dove-prism based image rotator for the coudé Tull spectrograph. Atmospheric dispersion produces wavelength-dependent shifts that increase with zenith distance; across 350–1000 nm, the displacement reaches ~3.5″ at a 60° zenith angle, reducing throughput away from the guiding wavelength. The RADC employs counter-rotating Amici prisms to provide continuous chromatic correction, while the Dove rotator stabilizes the instrument position angle and mitigates field rotation during long exposures on non-point-like targets. Together, these subsystems support consistent slit illumination and improved spectral fidelity. We summarize the optical and mechanical design approach, integration considerations, and expected gains in throughput and image stability.

Items.Authors: Reuben Neate, Tinus Stander, Roelf Botha
Items.Title: Packaging and deployment of a lightweight, low-cost, water vapour radiometer for site surveying
Items.Abstract: We present the latest developments on PILCHARD, a K-band dual-channel, 24 / 31.4 GHz, planar integrated low-cost water vapour radiometer developed for site surveying. We present selected details of the instrument lab performance, packaging requirements and integration of the instrument into a larger weather station, as well as preliminary qualification data.

Items.Authors: Haisheng Zhao
Items.Title: Particle identification methods and results for the follow-up X-ray telescope onboard Einstein Probe
Items.Abstract: Background removal is an important issue in data reduction for the Follow-up X-ray Telescope (FXT) onboard the Einstein Probe (EP), particularly for the particle-induced background. The particle-induced background in the FXT comprises background directly caused by particles, as well as instrument events that are also due to particles. A new rejection method, which involves cluster identification, and threshold veto for number of hits in rows and columns, is applied to remove the particle-induced background. The remaining background can be eliminated by the event reconstruction algorithm and event veto in subsequent FXT data reduction. It is shown that their methods can achieve a background rejection eﬀiciency of > 99.8 %. Additionally, there has been a notable decrease in the number of spikes in the light curves of the FXT. Furthermore, we found the instrument background is attributed to a combination of particles and CAMEX electronics.

Items.Authors: Elora Lefebvre, Marcel Carbillet, Olivier Lai, Lyu Abe, François-Xavier Schmider, Nhu Tin Mai, Julien Dejonghe, Jean-Pierre Rivet
Items.Title: Performance assessment of the AOC system on a 1-m telescope: stellar mode characterisation and planetary mode development
Items.Abstract: The AOC (Adaptive Optics at Calern) system aims to bring AO correction to 1-m class telescopes, which typically lack such capabilities, enhancing their high-angular resolution imaging performance. It offers both stellar (8.5″ FoV) and planetary (30.5″/80.5″ FoV) modes, guiding either on point sources or extended objects (such as Jupiter or Saturn). In the latter case, it introduces a filtering of the high-altitude turbulence, similar to ground-layer AO averaging, because high-altitude turbulence will be different around the edges of the planet, distorting the planetary disk, but not necessarily shifting the overall centroid.    This work focuses on the ongoing characterisation and optimisation of the system, from near-infrared to visible wavelengths. We are developing both simulation tools and diagnostic/evaluation tool, and comparing simulations, telemetry, and on-sky data, aiming at refining wavefront control and improving robustness for both stellar and planetary observations.

Items.Authors: Hannarong Janthaloet, Phichet Kittara, Dan Singwong, Chayanin Larkaew, Pichate Pha-kham, Siritida Duangbuppha, Pattanaphong Janphuang, Boon-Kok Tan, Ghassan Yassin, Kuan-Yu Liu, Ming-Jye Wang
Items.Title: Performance evaluation of a 230 GHz end-fire unilateral finline SIS mixer for large array receivers
Items.Abstract: We report on the development of a 230 GHz end-fire unilateral finline SIS mixer designed to upgrade the Heterodyne Array Receiver Program (HARP) on the James Clerk Maxwell Telescope (JCMT). Replacing the current probe-antenna design, this prototype targets the 180–250 GHz range (~30% bandwidth). We characterized the device using I-V measurements and the Y-factor technique. The results demonstrate clear photon-assisted tunneling steps and a distinct response between hot and cold loads, confirming operational efficiency. This work validates the finline architecture as a key step toward scaling the design to the 350 GHz band. Ultimately, this upgrade aims to significantly improve HARP’s sensitivity and widen the IF bandwidth for next-generation high-frequency observations.

Items.Authors: Mohammad N. Islam, Xuan Du, Timothy Robishaw, Sean Heakes, Mehak Parihar
Items.Title: Performance modelling for radio telescopes: an integrated framework of metrology, finite element analysis and electromagnetic simulation
Items.Abstract: This paper introduces an integrated framework that merges finite element analysis, drone-based photogrammetry, and electromagnetic simulation to model radio telescope performance more accurately. Applied to the 26‑m John A. Galt Telescope, verified FEA models predict structural deformation from gravity and temperature, while drone-based photogrammetry measures surface deviations and feed misalignments and add ground references. These real-world data are used in electromagnetic simulation to evaluate beam shape and polarization changes at various positions. The workflow supports structurally informed optimization and enhances telescope precision and reliability

Items.Authors: Malcolm C. Scarrott, Yuk Shan Cheng, Jake Charsley, Richard A. McCracken, Derryck T. Reid, Lisa A. Crause, Daniel L. Holdsworth, William Newman, Willem J. van der Westhuizen, Etienne L. Simon
Items.Title: Performance of the laser frequency comb for the red channel of SALT's High-Resolution spectrograph
Items.Abstract: We report on the completion of the integration and initial testing of a bespoke laser frequency comb (LFC) for the red channel (555-890 nm) of the High-Resolution Spectrograph (HRS) on the Southern African Large Telescope (SALT). The comb is driven by a 1 GHz Ti:sapphire laser, a photonic crystal fibre is used for supercontinuum generation, a plano-concave Fabry-Pérot cavity filters the modes to yield the required 20 GHz comb spacing and a spatial light modulator is employed in the spectral flattening module before comb light is delivered to the spectrograph via a single-mode fibre. A precision radial velocity data reduction pipeline has been written in Python to support the high-stability mode of the HRS that makes provision for simultaneous wavelength calibration. Future work aims to render the HRS LFC a turn-key system.

Items.Authors: Matteo Menessini, Simone Esposito, Lorenzo Busoni
Items.Title: Performance simulation of multi-stage XAO systems for high contrast imaging: RISTRETTO and beyond
Items.Abstract: The performance of the next generation of instruments for high contrast imaging on ground telescopes relies on the correction provided by an extreme adaptive optics (XAO) system. In this contribution, we study, through end-to-end simulations, the performance of a multi-stage XAO system to enable high contrast at small angular separations. We focus on the wavefront sensing and control aspect of the problem, optimizing the XAO loop upstream the coronograph to maximize contrast in the post-coronographic PSF. Existing AO loop algorithms and strategies are adapted to this new merit function. We consider different telescope apertures and coronograph types, concluding with the simulated performance tailored to the dual-stage system for RISTRETTO, a high-resolution IFU spectrograph proposed for the VLT.

Items.Authors: Miguel Andrés Sánchez Carrasco, Stefan Cikota, Marina Centenera-Merino, Javier Flores, Pedro José Amado-González, Jesús Aceituno-Castro, David Pérez-Medialdea, María Isabel Ruiz-López, Francisco José Pozuelos-Romero, Kalaga Madhav, Julius Göhring, Abani Shankar Nayak, Sergio León-Saval, José Luis Ortiz Moreno, Martin M. Roth
Items.Title: Photonic E-MARCOT at Calar Alto: architecture and integration of the MARCOT Pathfinder spectroscopic mode for on-sky validation of MM–MM photonic lanterns
Items.Abstract: The MARCOT Pathfinder is a multi-telescope demonstrator aimed at testing a scalable, fiber-fed spectroscopic architecture based on an array of small optical telescopes at Calar Alto Observatory. Its new spectroscopic mode combines post-focus fiber injection, a spectrograph focal adapter, and telescope control to provide stable coupling into an existing spectrograph interface. This contribution outlines the overall system architecture and the proposed on-sky validation of the spectroscopic mode under representative observing conditions at CAHA.

Items.Authors: Jacob H. Wirth, Alain Carrier, James Mason
Items.Title: Photonic integrated circuit heterodyne interferometer laser gauges for picometer-class metrology
Items.Abstract: The Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) has the ambitious goal of directly imaging and characterizing Exo-earths in search of life in the universe. For HWO to achieve this, the observatory requires a robust wavefront control system (WCS) to maintain wavefront stability to roughly 2 pm over up to 1000 seconds. As part of the larger WCS, HWO will employ a laser metrology truss consisting of many laser metrology gauges to measure the relative pose between the primary mirror segments and the secondary mirror. Lockheed Martin has developed laser metrology gauges with pm-class stability using photonic integrated circuit (PICs) heterodyne interferometers. In this presentation, we report experimental measurements of metrology errors internal to our PIC gauges. We also present an architecture study on placement and orientation of metrology gauges to minimize wavefront error. Additionally, we present a technology readiness level assessment and roadmap for achieving a level 5 for the gauges.

Items.Authors: Felipe Guzman
Items.Title: Picometer optical metrology for future space observatories
Items.Abstract: In this paper, we present the research work of the Laboratory of Space Systems and Optomechanics (LASSO) at the University of Arizona on laser-interferometric metrology technologies aimed at enabling picometer-level dimensional stability sensing and sub-nanoradian angular alignment for large, segmented space telescopes such as the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO). Central to this effort is the Optical Truss Interferometer (OTI), a compact and modular Fabry-Perot system that can be distributed across the telescope’s primary and secondary mirrors. Laboratory prototypes have demonstrated sub-picometer displacement sensitivity over representative baselines. Current work focuses on extending this performance to meter-scale cavity lengths while reducing the physical footprint and complexity of the optical heads. Altogether, this research addresses critical technology and metrology developments required for future missions like HWO, contributing toward NASA’s Exoplanet Exploration Program.

Items.Authors: Thomas Nikola, Amit Vishwas, Gordon J. Stacey, Baird Bankovic, Karwan Rostem, Alexander Kutyrev, Eric Mentzell, Jake Connors, Matias S. Calderon
Items.Title: POEMM: characterizing the spectral performance of the Virtually Imaged Phased Arrays for the short-wavelength and long-wavelength high-spectral resolution channels
Items.Abstract: POEMM is a balloon-borne NASA Pioneers mission to study the formation and evolution of planets in the far-IR wavelength range between 35 and 112 micron. In addition to a low resolution grating channel covering 35 to 70 micron, it has two high-resolution channels that are enabled by Virtually Imaged Phased Arrays (VIPAs). The VIPAs for POEMM consist of polished blocks of high-purity silicon onto which a ~200nm gold film is deposited. One of the two VIPAs will measure the H2O, HD, and [OI] lines between 40 and 63 micron with RP~50,000. The other VIPA will measure the 112 micron HD transition with RP~100,000. Here we present the two cryogenic testbeds to characterize the VIPAs. We elaborate on the mechanical design of the test cryostats, their optical layout, and the test results. The VIPA characterization measurements are done with the VIPAs cooled to 4K.

Items.Authors: Vincent Revéret, Louis Rodriguez, Albrecht Poglitsch, Eliana Recoba Pawlowski, Laurent Dussopt, Abdelkader Aliane, Valérie Goudon
Items.Title: Polarimetric all silicon bolometric arrays in the submillimeter domain: new results
Items.Abstract: We present the latest developments concerning BBOP detectors, a new generation of “instrument-in-pixel’’ bolometric arrays enabling high-sensitivity submillimeter polarimetry for astrophysical magnetic-field studies. Recent results show substantial sensitivity gains approaching the sub-attoW/√Hz regime at 50 mK, successful validation of the multiplexed readout system, and the first performance measurements at 350 µm, extending earlier 100 µm work. Their orthogonal antennae allow simultaneous Stokes parameter retrieval with fully differential outputs. These advances support upcoming POLARYS observations at APEX and establish BBOP arrays as key components for future balloon-borne and ground-based polarimetric instruments.

Items.Authors: Eduard R. Muslimov, Luca Fossati, Coralie Neiner, Jean-Claude Bouret, Davide Le Mignant, Kjetil Dohlen, Jean-Michel Reess, Adrien Girardot
Items.Title: POLLUX: optical architecture of a high-resolution spectrograph and polarimeter for the Habitable Worlds Observatory
Items.Abstract: POLLUX is a European project of a high-resolution spectrograph with polarimetric capabilities for the future Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO). Its current optical architecture implies splitting the instrument into five channels, each comprising an echelle spectrograph. The far UV channel provides spectropolarimetry in the 100-123 nm range. The medium UV channel can operate in spectropolarimetry mode in the 121.7-236 nm range or pure spectroscopy mode in the 100.6-236 nm range. The near UV channel covers the range 234-472 nm in spectroscopy or spectroplarimetry mode. The expected spectral resolving power, including a margin for manufacturing and assembly, is 90 000, 71 700 and 94 000 for the three UV channels, respectively. The visible (472-944 nm) and near infrared (944-1888 nm) are coupled via an optical fiber interface. They are designed to reach the resolving power of >70 000 in point-source spectroscopy/spectropolarimetry and will be considered in detail in a separate paper.

Items.Authors: Keigo Enya, Shingo Kameda
Items.Title: Possible contributions of Japan to the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO)
Items.Abstract: The Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) is NASA's planned flagship space telescope, following the James Webb Space Telescope and the Roman Space Telescope, of which launch is scheduled for the 2040s. The HWO will conduct observations in the ultraviolet (UV) to near-infrared (NIR) wavelength range using a 6-meter-class telescope. One of HWO's science goals is to search for Earth-like exoplanets (including the search for signs of life) using a coronagraph, and will also conduct astrophysical and astronomical observations possible in the UV to near-infrared wavelength range. The HWO is a NASA-led mission with an international partnership. At this moment, Japan is considering contributing to the HWO via science, the coronagraph hardware, and UV hardware. We present possible contributions of Japan to the HWO.

Items.Authors: Michael A. Reuter, Angelo Fausti, Amanda Ibsen, Tiago Ribeiro, Wouter van Reeven
Items.Title: Practical experience using Apache Kafka as the middleware for the Rubin Observatory control system
Items.Abstract: The Rubin Observatory Control System (Rubin-OCS) is a distributed system with each component in charge of a particular sub-system. Communication between the components is done by means of a software middleware. After the Kafka feasibility study was approved, implementation and testing proceeded for new Kafka based system. Prior to the start of the LSSTCam commissioning campaign, the observatory switched the middleware technology for the Rubin-OCS from DDS to Kafka. The switch to Kafka has allowed the observatory more flexibility to respond to requests for interface upgrades and stability of performance.

Items.Authors: Wenxin Wang, Donghua Zhao, Yuan Liu, Haiwu Pan, Zhixing Ling, Chen Zhang, Weimin Yuan, Shuang-Nan Zhang
Items.Title: Preliminary study of EP-WXT background using earth-occulted data
Items.Abstract: EP, launched on 9 January 2024, is a mission dedicated to time-domain high energy astrophysics. It carries two scientific payloads: the Wide-field X-ray Telescope (WXT) and the Follow-up X-ray Telescope (FXT). The EP-WXT consists of 12 identical modules and covers 1/11 of the sky in a single snapshot. Its energy band ranges from 0.5 to 4 keV. Each module contains lobster-eye micropore optics with scientific CMOS (sCMOS) focal-plane detectors. In this work, we present preliminary results of the EP-WXT background analysis using earth-occulted data.

Items.Authors: Manasa Lakshmi Narasimhan, Nicole Melso, David Schiminovich, Rain Naylor
Items.Title: Prototype spectropolarimetry module for lenslet-based integral field spectrographs: design and calibration
Items.Abstract: Integral-field spectropolarimetry enables simultaneous spatial, spectral, and polarization measurements. In tandem with spectral information, polarized emission can be used to map the kinematics of dust expelled from galaxies and to probe the underlying spectrum of scattered light. Our work showcases a prototype design of a compact, off-the-shelf, optical polarization module intended for pairing with lenslet-based integral-field spectrographs, like the Circumgalactic Hα Spectrograph. We describe the opto-mechanical layout, data collection scheme, and the strategies used to measure and calibrate possible instrumental polarization. The module enables polarization measurements without requiring major modifications to the optical path and allows for compatibility with existing IFU spectrographs. We will present the design, implementation, and laboratory characterization of this prototype, highlighting its role in enabling future integral field spectropolarimetric measurements.

Items.Authors: Anthony Berdeu, Jean-Baptiste Le Bouquin, Henri M. Bonnet, Sylvain Oberti, Johann Kolb, Julien Woillez, Guillaume Bourdarot, Thibaut Paumard, Frank Eisenhauer, Christian Straubmeier, Paulo Garcia, Sebastian Hönig, Florentin Millour, Denis Defrère, Férréol Soulez
Items.Title: Pseudo-synthetic interaction matrix for the GRAVITY+ Adaptive Optics system: modeling and calibration of the ALPAO deformable mirror influence functions and coupling
Items.Abstract: The GRAVITY+ Adaptive Optics systems at the Very Large Telescope are based on 43x43 deformable mirrors  (DM), under-resolved by the different Shack-Hartmann wavefront sensors: 9x9 infrared, 40x40 visible and 30x30  laser guide star. Having a fine model of the DM is crucial to control its shape and ensure that the low order  modes of the control basis do not produce unseen high spatial frequencies. We present how we obtain a two-  dimensional super-resolved model of the DM mean influence function and how we calibrate its coupling matrix.  This allows to produce almost pure low order modes with negligible loss of performances.

Items.Authors: Grace Sweetak, Breann Sitarski, Kevin France, Randall McEntaffer
Items.Title: PyISH: python integral field spectrograph simulation for HWO
Items.Abstract: The Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) is a large ultraviolet/optical/near-infrared space telescope recommended by the National Academies’ Astro2020 decadal survey. The most recent HWO architectural studies have added an ultraviolet integral field spectrograph (IFS) to the baseline instrument suite. To understand the trade between different instrument parameters, such as spectral and spatial resolution and field of view, we developed PyISH, a UV IFS simulation tool. PyISH models the components of a UV IFS and allows users to provide a broad range of input science cases. The simulation outputs UV IFS-related deliverables, including a three-dimensional data cube based on user-specified input parameters. PyISH provides the user with the ability to explore engineering trades to directly link engineering constraints with science deliverables. PyISH’s components and applications to science, engineering, and HWO will be described in this presentation.

Items.Authors: Martin Baláž, Kieran Leschinski, Gilles Otten, Oliver Czoske, Janus Brink, Jennifer Karr, Benjamin Eisele, Hugo Buddelmeijer, Thomas Marquart, Wolfgang Kausch
Items.Title: Pythonic pipeline framework compatible with ESO software stack
Items.Abstract: In 2023, ESO approved the use of Python in instrument software packages,  enabling developers to work at a higher level of abstraction  than was possible with legacy C code. This transition supports  improved code reuse and modularity and the decoupling of the general principles of data-reduction pipelines  from the scientific objectives of individual instruments. Pipeline developers can therefore  focus on instrument-specific requirements and abstract away the complexities of managing the data flow.    In this poster, we present a generic Python framework for building data-processing pipelines.  The framework is fully compatible with the existing ESO software stack (EDPS, pyesorex)  while keeping dependencies to minimum in order to allow independent use,  and is already being employed to implement the data-reduction pipeline for METIS at ELT,  potentially paving the way for broader adoption across future instruments.

Items.Authors: Jordan D. Wheeler, Anna K. Vaskuri, Jason Austermann, Michael Vissers, Johannes Hubmayr, Shannon Duff, Matthew Koc, Joel Ullom, Simon Doyle, Thomas L. R. Brien, Michael L. Brown
Items.Title: Quasi-lumped element matching of superconducting transmission lines to MKIDs
Items.Abstract: Multichroic, wide-bandwidth millimeter and submillimeter focal planes often require on-chip circuitry to separate astronomical signals spectrally. When using a microwave kinetic inductance detector (MKID), coupling to the mm-wave circuit must be made directly to the MKID inductor. A difficulty is that typical MKID materials have resistances on the order of 1 ohm/square or higher, resulting in a large reactance in the lossy transmission line formed by the MKID inductor. This imaginary part of the impedance is challenging to match to the purely real impedance of a lossless superconducting transmission line. However, complex loads can be matched with lumped elements over a limited bandwidth. As such, we explore coupling schemes employing quasi-lumped-element matching networks, some of which do not require galvanic contact between the transmission line and MKID inductor. These matching networks expand the potential to achieve high detector absorption with fewer constraints on the MKID.

Items.Authors: Benjamin J. Weiner, Grant Williams, Timothy Pickering, Dallan Porter, J. Duane Gibson, Sean Moran
Items.Title: Queue Scheduling and Observing with Binospec and MMIRS at the MMT Observatory
Items.Abstract: Binospec and MMIRS are optical and IR wide-field spectrographs operated in queue mode at the MMT Observatory in Arizona, currently queue scheduled for 100-120 nights/semester. PIs design observations, slitmasks, and upload targets for Binospec and MMIRS through web interfaces run by MMT and SAO. At night, a scheduling program ranks observing blocks, from which the queue observers choose targets appropriate to conditions. Pipelines run by SAO scientists return reduced data to the PIs through the web interface. MMT instrument scientists support both the PIs and QOs as intermediaries. Queue observing has many advantages for flexibility, especially for time domain astronomy and targets of opportunity. However, it separates the PIs from the observing process, adding pressure on observation design to communicate the science goals, and on the observatory to manage PI expectations. We will discuss the Observatory Manager web interfaces and some of the common pinch points in queue operations.

Items.Authors: sini yang, Lin Wen, Qihang Han, Yonghe Chen, Dongge Zhang, Jian Ge, Haijiao Jiang
Items.Title: Radiation-induced performance degradation of optical materials for the Earth 2.0 space mission
Items.Abstract: This study evaluates the radiation tolerance of five optical materials—fused silica, CaF₂, H-LaF10, H-ZF1, and H-ZBaF20—for the Earth 2.0 transit telescopes. Ground-based experiments simulated electron, gamma-ray, and proton irradiation at L2 and measured transmission degradation over 450–960 nm. Results show strong variation in radiation sensitivity: fused silica performed best (<1.5% degradation), while heavy lanthanum glasses were most sensitive, with gamma-ray damage up to 18.3%. Proton irradiation caused the most severe overall degradation. Sequential irradiation produced less damage than cumulative estimates. Findings provide critical data for radiation-resistant optical design of space-based photometric instruments.

Items.Authors: José Marco de La Rosa, Josefina Rosich, Oscar Tubío, Alastair Basden, Jesús Patrón, Iciar Montilla, Roberto López, Marta Puga, Roberto Simoes, Eduardo González, Manuel Luis, Héctor De Paz, Manuel Huertas, Sergio Fernández, Gianluca Lombardi, Marcos Reyes, Víctor Béjar
Items.Title: Real-Time Control Software for the AO Loops of GTCAO
Items.Abstract: GTCAO’s adaptive optics system relies on a real-time AO control loop that senses and reconstructs the wavefront to drive a deformable mirror. To enhance performance and durability, the system includes two additional offloading loops: tip-tilt offload to M2 and global wavefront plus segment tip-tilt offload to M1.  This work presents the architecture of the software that implements these real-time loops and the components interfacing with the telescope’s active optics. It also summarizes the operational software, GUIs, simulators, and calibration and performance tools currently running in production at the GTC. Key conclusions and lessons learned from the development process are included.

Items.Authors: Robert L. Johnson
Items.Title: Recent advances in sodium beacon development
Items.Abstract: Scientists at Starfire Optical Range (SOR) have been researching Rayleigh and sodium beacons for adaptive optics (AO) for over 30 years. In 2016, we combined light from two 22 W sodium lasers to form a single beacon. These commercial lasers use resonant-frequency doubling of light from a Raman fiber-amplifier. In 2019, we started to develop a 75 W sodium laser for better correction of turbulence in poor seeing. We increased the beacon return flux by chirping the laser wavelength to compensate for recoil of optically pumped sodium atoms. In addition, we have demonstrated a single-sideband D2b re-pumper. In this talk, we discuss results from on-sky tests in 2025 that demonstrate improvement in beacon brightness by using these techniques. We also discuss sodium beacon research in low-cost semiconductor lasers, novel techniques for higher laser power, and uplink compensation to reduce the size of the beacon in the mesosphere, thereby improving sensitivity of the wavefront measurement.

Items.Authors: Juan Carlos Trelles Arjona, Carlos Quintero Noda, Manuel Collados Vera, Silvia Regalado Olivares, Patricia Gómez González, Antonio Matta, Jonai Bienes, Jorge Quintero-Nehrkorn, Mary Barreto, María Jesús Martínez González
Items.Title: Recent updates and status of the Gregor Infrared spectrograph
Items.Abstract: The GREGOR Infrared Spectrograph, installed at the GREGOR solar telescope at the Observatorio del Teide, began operations in 2012 and has undergone several upgrades over the years. It is currently undergoing its most significant upgrade to date, which includes, among other improvements, the addition of two new optical channels to enable simultaneous multi-wavelength observations. The second arm was successfully integrated and made available to the community from the 2024 campaign, providing exciting and novel results. Moreover, work continues to ensure that the third channel could be installed and operating by the beginning of the 2026 observing campaign. In this contribution, we present observation highlights thanks to the new upgrades, with special emphasis on the first results from the integration of the third channel. Finally, we outline the future upgrades planned to ensure the instrument remains aligned with ongoing developments in solar physics and instrumentation.

Items.Authors: Frederick S. Porter, Renata Cumbee, Megan E. Eckart, Ryuichi Fujimoto, Yoshitaka Ishisaki, Yoshiaki Kanemaru, Richard L. Kelley, Caroline A. Kilbourne, Maurice Leutenegger, Michael Loewenstein, Yoshitomo Maeda, Misaki Mizumoto, Kosuke Sato, Makoto Sawada, Russell Shipman, Yoh Takei, Masahiro Tsujimoto, Yuusuke Uchida, Shinya Yamada
Items.Title: Reconstructing the time dependent energy scale for XRISM/Resolve instrument on orbit
Items.Abstract: The Resolve instrument on the XRISM observatory has performed exceptionally well since its launch in September 2023, performing substantially better than its requirements. A key part of this success has been the reconstruction of the time-dependent energy scale, on-orbit. Instrumental conditions that affect the gain include the 50mK heat sink temperature, bolometric loading, thermal crosstalk within the instrument, and variations in the temperature of the warm electronics. Most of these effects are time dependent. A great deal of planning and development effort was dedicated to ensuring that the time-dependent gain would be correctable on-orbit. Much of that planning had to be reformulated when the instrument gate valve remained closed. However, we have developed a robust methodology for energy scale reconstruction on-orbit that results in uncertainties that are an order of magnitude better than the requirement. This strongly affects the scientific output of the mission.

Items.Authors: Francesco Di Mille, David Osip, Lionel Zumaran, Povilas Palunas
Items.Title: Remote Observing with the Magellan Telescopes
Items.Abstract: Remote observing at the Magellan Telescopes has evolved into a robust and efficient mode of operation supporting a wide range of programs. Observers prepare their runs in advance through a dedicated online system and connect on observing nights through a system that mirrors the control-room experience at Las Campanas Observatory. With real-time live communication with operators and support astronomers, remote users can monitor the telescope state, carry out calibrations, and execute their observing plans as if they were on site.    The system was designed to preserve the collaborative nature of classical Magellan observing while offering the flexibility required for distributed research teams. This poster will describe the system architecture, operational model, and user experience, along with lessons learned from its adoption at Magellan.

Items.Authors: Haoyang Zhang, Yingfu Wang, Jiahao Zhou, Wengfei Liu, Mengmeng Qian, Xianke Song, Kai Yun, Hongzhuan Hu, Jiangping Wang, Jiaru Chu, Ping Zhang, Zhigang Liu, Zengxiang Zhou
Items.Title: Research on photogrammetric reference based on high-density miniature fiber positioners
Items.Abstract: The LAMOST closed-loop detection system employs a 21mm diameter fiducial fibers. To accommodate the upcoming 10.4mm aperture grouped fiber solution, it's crucial to provide a detection reference for tens of thousands of grouped fiber positioner. This project focuses on researching a high-precision measurement benchmark scheme and designing a reference fiber unit adapted to the 10.4mm aperture focal plane, meeting the current system's demand for high-precision closed-loop detection. The challenge lies in further optimizing and reducing the size of the existing reference fiber unit, which is already quite compact, without affecting its fundamental functions and ensuring the uniformity and stability of the emitted light spot. This design scheme will contribute to more accurate fiber position determination by photogrammetry, improve the stability of the detection system, and ensure the overall reliable operation of the telescope.

Items.Authors: Christoph Baranec, Reed Riddle, James Ou, Suzanne Zhang, Zachary Werber, Guillaume Huber, Luke Mckay, Rachel Rampy, Mark Chun, Michael Liu, Keith Powell, Marcos A. van Dam
Items.Title: Robo-AO-2: entering the era of automated science operations, hybrid wavefront sensing, and adaptive secondary integration
Items.Abstract: We present the first science results and new technical milestones from the Robo-AO-2 facility at the University of Hawaii 2.2-m telescope. Following successful commissioning, the system commenced science operations in 2025. We are starting a large-scale survey of 2500 young stars in the Scorpius–Centaurus association to detect sub-stellar companions, vetting the Habitable Worlds Observatory Target Stars and Systems (TSS25) list, discovering stellar blends for TESS exoplanet host candidates, locating transients in their host galaxies, and executing surveys of main-belt asteroid families. We report on the commissioning of the natural guide star wavefront sensor, now supporting science and hybrid laser-stellar sensing demonstrations. Finally, we detail the automation of the telescope facility, Robo88, via updated telescope control systems and absolute encoders, and the integration of Robo-AO-2 with the telescope's new adaptive secondary mirror.

Items.Authors: Alessandro Attoli, Franco Buffa, Francesco Gaudiomonte, Giampaolo Serra, Sergio Poppi, Antonietta Fara, Pasqualino Marongiu, Mauro Pili, Gian Paolo Vargiu, Giannina Sanna, Gian Luigi Deiana
Items.Title: Sardinia Radio Telescope Metrology System: early commissioning insights
Items.Abstract: Two years after the completion of its high frequency enhancement, the Sardinia Radio Telescope has returned to scientific operations with renewed capabilities, enabling the antenna system to operate up to 116 GHz.  However, observing at the maximum frequency for which the SRT was designed, requires a tighter control of both antenna pointing and main reflector surface accuracy, considering the contribution of environmental loads on its structural behaviour.  The Sardinia Radio Telescope Metrology System (SMS), designed to support the SRT high frequency observations, is fully installed and ready for commissioning tests which are currently under way.  In this regard, the paper summarises the progress achieved over the last two years, describing the activities carried out to characterise tools and instrumentation devoted to metrology applications and presenting the preliminary results.

Items.Authors: Daniel Küsters, Greg Aldering, Benjamin Bastian-Querner, Marek Kowalski, Marko Kossatz, Saul Perlmutter, David Rubin
Items.Title: SCALA 2.0: towards NIST-traceable standard stars using SNIFS
Items.Abstract: Enhanced calibration accuracy for the SuperNova Integral Field Spectrograph (SNIFS) has been enabled by a substantial upgrade to the SNIFS CALibration Apparatus (SCALA) flux calibration source at the University of Hawai‘i 88-inch telescope on Maunakea. Here we discuss the installation of the upgraded system and present measurements obtained using it. These demonstrate the anticipated rejection of out-of-band light, greatly reduced scatted light, and better background subtraction for day-time measurements. Since the reinstallation we have monitored the relative changes between the 18 installed photodiodes, finding that the sensitivity of one of them has evolved. We conclude by showing how SCALA is aiding us in understanding details of SNIFS, needed for the development of a forward model for data extraction.

Items.Authors: Barry Rothberg, Edward J. Montiel, Brian D. Mason, Rachel A. Matson, Kimberly A. Rupley, Daniel R. Veillette
Items.Title: Science and the City: Astronomical Observations from the US Capital
Items.Abstract: The United States Naval Observatory (USNO) was established by Congress in 1842 & moved to its current location north of Georgetown in 1893. It is one of the oldest continually operating astronomical institutes in the United States. The site has hosted a number of notable telescopes and surveys including the 26" Great Equatorial refractor, the 1.0m RC reflector, and the USNO CCD Astrograph Catalog. Although USNO began operating a field station in Arizona in the mid-1950s, astronomical observations never stopped in Washington D.C. We present an overview of scientific work done at USNO DC, highlighting the ongoing work of the 26-inch Great Equatorial refractor & the Washington Double Star Catalog; the 70cm Capital Astronomical Telescope which is capable of rapid follow-up to transient events and wide area surveys; and the remote operation of the 1.0m Deep South Telescope in Chile. Despite being in the heart of Washington D.C., it continues to make notable contributions to astronomy.

Items.Authors: Goeun Kim, Jongguk Choe, Youngchun Youk, Jeeyeon Yoon, Eung Shik Lee, Haeng Pal Heo
Items.Title: Sensitivity and tolerance analysis of a drag-reduced compact Korsch telescope for low-altitude small-satellite missions
Items.Abstract: Space telescopes operating in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) are directly affected by atmospheric drag, which significantly impacts their orbital lifetime. This study designed a Compact Korsch telescope considering drag reduction by minimizing the frontal area exposed to the orbital direction. This results in closer distance between the primary and secondary mirrors, which increases sensitivity to alignment errors. This paper presents systematic sensitivity and tolerance analyses comparing the conventional and drag-reduced Korsch designs, examining the feasibility of drag-reduced telescope design for low-altitude missions.

Items.Authors: Freek Roelofs, Heino Falcke
Items.Title: SHARPEx: the first space-to-space VLBI experiment
Items.Abstract: Space is the next frontier for ultra-high resolution imaging with very long baseline interferometry (VLBI). The limited size of the Earth and atmospheric absorption and turbulence at high frequencies prevent order-of-magnitude resolution improvements from current black hole imaging with the Event Horizon Telescope. A three-element submm space-based array like SHARP would image the thin black hole photon ring and measure the black hole spin and spacetime. Here, we present the SHARP Experiment (SHARPEx) mission concept. SHARPEx will demonstrate key enabling technologies for space-to-space VLBI, including clock synchronization between two satellites, on-board correlation, and sub-wavelength orbit determination. SHARPEx will consist of two CubeSat or SmallSat platforms carrying small (~1 m) antennas, observing at cm wavelengths. Depending on the intersatellite link properties (range and bandwidth), SHARPEx may produce images of bright AGN with unprecedented resolution and fidelity.

Items.Authors: Alessandro Lorenzetto, Davide Ricci, Fulvio Laudisio, Daniele Vassallo, Andrea Baruffolo, Domenico Barbato, Maria Bergomi, Elena Carolo, Paolo Cerpelloni, Simone Di Filippo, Valentina D'Orazi, Cecilia Lazzoni, Tânia Sofia Gomes Machado, Davide Greggio, Luca Marafatto, Lorenzo Merli, Dino Mesa, Jacopo Farinato
Items.Title: SHINS-OBS : diving in SHARK-NIR's new UI for deep remote access and control.
Items.Abstract: SHARK-NIR instrument (System for coronagraphy with high-order AO in Z and H band) is a high-contrast coronagraph imager mounted at the LBT. The instrument's early science verification phase highlighted the necessity for a user-friendly and remotely accessible interface. This was driven by the complex operations required to fully exploit the AO capabilities and successfully complete an observation run. The new web based user interface is presented in all its new features, highlighting the new custom OB-Editor able to prepare all the detailed observing blocks starting from the essential information provided by science case, the immediate control of adaptive optics device and the new direct access to diagnostic data from technical and scientific cameras.  New features of the instrument such as the automatic rotation of the Non Common Path Aberrations following the field derotation are also presented

Items.Authors: Marc-Antoine Martinod, Vincent Foriel, Nick Cvetojevic, Frantz Martinache, Jeronimo Calderon-Gomez, Roxanne Ligi, David Mary
Items.Title: Silencing the stellar glare with kernel-nulling and active phase control on photonic chips
Items.Abstract: Characterizing exoplanets and finding biosignatures are among the hottest topics in astronomy. This quest is challenged by the brightness contrast between the faint planet and the overwhelming glare of the host star, their small angular separation, and observing conditions degraded by optical aberrations. Nulling interferometry is a promising technique to achieve this goal by fulfilling requirements for both high contrast and high angular resolution. Photonic-Integrated Circuits (PICs) provide compactness, design versatility, and scalability needed for nulling. With the PHOTONICS project, we aim to create novel coherent combination architectures, based on a multimode interferometer (MMI) coupler and on-chip active phase control with no moving parts. We will present the first lab tests of a 4-beam kernel-nuller made out of a single MMI coupler with active phase control: ABCD fringe-tracking and the characterization of the contrast detection limits of a four-beam kernel-nuller.

Items.Authors: Corey Spohn, Christopher C. Stark
Items.Title: Simulating images for a complete HWO survey with coronagraphoto
Items.Abstract: Evaluating the end-to-end performance of coronagraph designs for HWO will require simulations that span a full multi-year mission timeline. Such simulations must capture instrument performance, evolving astrophysical scenes, and post-processing, generating data volumes that push the limits of current tools. To address this challenge we have developed a new pipeline by linking a new image simulation tool called coronagraphoto to existing HWO mission simulation tools. We will present images representing a complete, multi-year simulated observing campaign by a preliminary HWO design. The dataset consists of thousands of individual frames over multiple photometric bands, capturing the orbital motion of multi-planet systems and multiple noise sources. This work will provide a vital dataset for testing post-processing algorithms and performing trade studies between HWO coronagraph designs. We plan to make this complete dataset publicly available.

Items.Authors: Radhika Dharmadhikari, Aurelie Magniez, Charlotte Bond, Padmakar Parihar, Kieran O'Brien, Tim Morris
Items.Title: Simulations on petal mode sensing for the ELT using the OTF based-phasing scheme
Items.Abstract: The large spiders in the ELT lead to phase discontinuities of the wavefront, which appear as a piston difference between two sectors of the primary mirror. The adaptive optics system is insensitive to large values of these petal modes and hence a special petalometer device is required, that can measure these petal modes.  We have explored the use of Optical Transfer Function (OTF) based phasing scheme for fast petal mode sensing of the ELT. The performance of this technique under varying external practical conditions for seeing limited as well as AO corrected mode are studied through realistic Python simulations.

Items.Authors: Lukas Weissinger, Bernadett Stadler, Simon Hubmer, Ronny Ramlau
Items.Title: Singular value-based Atmospheric tomography with Fourier domain Regularization (SAFR)
Items.Abstract: Atmospheric tomography, the problem of reconstructing atmospheric turbulence profiles from wavefront sensor measurements, is an integral part of many adaptive optics systems. To solve this problem, a singular-value decomposition (SVD) based approach has been proposed before. Here, we focus on the numerical implementation of the SVD-based Atmospheric Tomography with Fourier Domain Regularization Algorithm (SAFR) and its performance for MCAO systems. The key features of the SAFR algorithm are the utilization of the FFT and the pre-computation of computationally demanding parts. Together, this yields a fast algorithm with less memory requirements than commonly used Matrix Vector Multiplication (MVM) approaches. We evaluate the performance of SAFR regarding reconstruction quality and computational expense in numerical experiments using the simulation environment COMPASS, in which we use an MCAO setup resembling the physical parameters of the MORFEO instrument of the ELT.

Items.Authors: Emanuele Perinati, Michael J. Freyberg, Michael C. Yeung, Konrad Dennerl, Christian Pommranz, Susanne Friedrich, Ritika Singh, Bastian Hess, Sebastian Diebold, Chris Tenzer, Andrea Santangelo
Items.Title: Soft proton induced background in SRG/eROSITA: a follow-up study
Items.Abstract: The X-ray telescope eROSITA aboard the SRG spacecraft provided measurements of instrumental background at L2, that can be used to acquire knowledge about the experienced radiation environment. In this paper, we aim to make the previously published picture on soft protons more complete by presenting some results from the analysis of eRASS5 background data. We also compare background data taken in fully open position of the filter-wheel (i.e. without external filter) during a PV-phase observation with that in closed position.

Items.Authors: Zhiyuan Ma, Grant Wilson, Itziar Aretxaga, Daniela Espitia-Mosquera, Joseph Golec, Michael McCrackan, Alfredo Montaña, Kamal Souccar
Items.Title: Software Framework for TolTEC Operation and Data Automation
Items.Abstract: The TolTEC Camera, mounted on the Large Millimeter Telescope (LMT), is a continuum imaging polarimeter that simultaneously observers at 1.1, 1.4, and 2.0 mm wavelengths. TolTECA v3 is the third major release of the TolTEC data handling software stack that facilitates the TolTEC operation and TolTEC data automation. In this version, we rewrite the data model implementation using the a schema-driven design focusing on structured metadata, and the tolteca_db submodule is now a separate dedicated package built on top of the data models, providing layered API endpoints for interacting with the data acquisition system, initializing data ingestion tasks, orchestration of data reduction pipelines, and working as the visualization tooling backend, both during observing and during post-data analysis sessions. With TolTECA v3, TolTEC operation is fully automated throughout the data and data product lifecycle from raw data ingestion to data product management.

Items.Authors: Fabrizio Vitali
Items.Title: SOXS at the NTT: installation and commissioning of the NIR arm
Items.Abstract: SOXS (Son Of X-Shooter) is a single object spectrograph, built by an international consortium for the 3.58-m ESO New Technology Telescope at the La Silla Observatory. It offers a simultaneous spectral coverage over 350-2000 nm, with two separate spectrographs. SOXS is currently mounted at the Nasmyth focus of NTT and, at the time of writing, is completing the technical and scientific commissioning. In this paper we describe the status and the performances of the Near InfraRed arm, as derived from the commissioning in Chile.

Items.Authors: Salvatore Savarese, Marco Landoni, David Young, Davide Ricci, Stephen Smartt, Paolo D'Avanzo, Sergio Campana, Pietro Schipani, Matteo Aliverti, José A. Araiza-Durán, Iair Arcavi, Andrea Baruffolo, Federico Battaini, Sagi Ben-Ami, Alex Bichkovsky, Anna Brucalassi, Giulio Capasso, Enrico Cappellaro, Riccardo Claudi, Mirko Colapietro, Rosario Cosentino, Francesco D'Alessio, Sergio D'Orsi, Massimo Della Valle, Simone Di Filippo, Avishay Gal-Yam, Matteo Genoni, Ofir Hershko, Hanindyo Kuncarayakti, Luigi Lessio, Laurent Marty, Seppo Mattila, Matteo Munari, Giuliano Pignata, Kalyan Radhakrishnan, Michael Rappaport, Marco Riva, Adam Rubin, Bernardo Salasnich, Maximilian Stritzinger, Fabrizio Vitali, Ricardo Zanmar Sánchez, Salvatore Scuderi
Items.Title: SOXS Quality Control System for Operations at the NTT
Items.Abstract: The SOXS spectrograph at the ESO NTT has completed its AIV and Commissioning phases, and a dedicated Quality Control (QC) system is required to monitor performance during routine operations. Daily calibration and engineering data acquired by the ICS are processed by the SOXS pipeline, which produces science outputs and a set of diagnostic parameters describing throughput, resolution, detector behaviour and other key metrics.  These parameters are ingested into ESO Datalab, used as the central service for storing and visualising QC information. Datalab provides scalable storage, dashboard tools and programmatic access integrated with the ESO software environment. The resulting QC system allows the operations team and the community to follow temporal trends and compare them with commissioning baselines. This contribution presents the QC architecture, dataflow and current implementation as SOXS enters regular operations at the NTT.

Items.Authors: Carmelo Arcidiacono, Matteo Simioni, Simone Zaggia, Patrizia Borin, Luca Cortese, Marco Dima, Rosanna Sordo, Marco Gullieuszik
Items.Title: Space Surveillance Awareness programme at Ekar Observatory
Items.Abstract: The Cima Ekar Observatory (INAF–OAPd) has launched a new operational programme for Space Surveillance and Awareness, combining the robotic Schmidt telescope with the Copernico 1.82-m telescope equipped with AFOSC. Within the ASI–INAF agreement on space-debris monitoring, we are upgrading both sensors and developing coordinated photometric, astrometric, and spectroscopic workflows to characterise objects from LEO to GEO. The Schmidt provides wide-field, dynamically scheduled imaging for orbit determination and light-curve analysis, while AFOSC enables targeted spectroscopic and multi-band characterisation. We describe the operational model, data-flow integration with IA2 archives, early performance results, and the roadmap toward supporting national SSA activities and future Fly-Eye operations.
